capabilities: Store API tokens and values encrypted under a master password
Insert secret keys into notes with autocomplete and placeholder syntax
Proxy AI agents' HTTP requests, replacing keys and masking values in responses
Expose notes tagged as MCP tools for connected AI clients
Show a live activity log of every AI client request and approval
extras: Desktop only (Obsidian 1.13+) because the local server needs Node.js APIs unavailable on mobile. No password recovery: forgetting the master password loses the stored variables. Free and open source, no telemetry or account; README documents security limits such as malicious plugins sharing the same process.
problem: AI agents working with Obsidian need API credentials, but pasting tokens into notes or exposing them to agents risks leaking them; this plugin keeps values encrypted and brokers requests instead.

relations.evidence: Environment Keys registers as a module on AI Ecosystem's unified local server (127.0.0.1:27150)
Claude Code: runs claude mcp add --transport http --scope user environment-variables
Cursor: adds an environment-variables entry to ~/.cursor/mcp.json

requires.name: AI client (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Cursor or any MCP client)

summary: Secret vault that stores API tokens encrypted in the vault and lets AI agents use them in HTTP requests through a local MCP server without seeing the values.
